brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three bases arranged around an empty spot
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at (1,0), (2,0) and (0,1) at level 0. Each touches the empty cell (1,1), which is the spot left open for the bay. (1,0)-(2,0) and (1,0)-(0,1) are adjacent, so they form a chain around the spot.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in that empty spot
requirements.evidence: Full bay tray (solid, north bay, ref bay:0#1,1#bay1, stem hex-bin-bay-n-full-solid) bolted at empty cell (1,1). check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no rule errors (only an info note about possible caps).

finish.summary: Built three full hex bases at (1,0), (2,0), (0,1) surrounding the empty cell (1,1), with a solid full bay tray seated in that spot. The configurator reports no errors and a clear mesh check. Note: the bay's offer only appeared once the three bases surrounded the empty cell. A base at (0,0) I'd started with was removed to make room for this layout. The three bases are not all mutually adjacent (they form a chain of two adjacencies around the spot), which is what the bay offer accepted.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
